run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:04:22Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend-proxy RequestErrorRate alert is explained by its own 504 upstream timeouts: frontend-proxy ingress spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR rose from 0 (point 01:03:22) to ~289–607 per 5m from 01:05:22 through 01:13:22, and its p95 ingress duration jumped from ~400–500 ms to the 15000 ms bucket top at 01:05:22. Its logs show '504 UT response_timeout' with 15000 ms durations for GET /api/products/*, GET /api/recommendations and POST /api/checkout against upstream 'frontend'. The dependency that was faulted is product-catalog: chaos-mesh events record NetworkChaos experiments named otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-* created by the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay that 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' every minute from 01:02:21Z to 01:10:21Z (each recovered ~55 s later). Frontend's own spans confirm the failing edge: grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client spans failed with rpc.grpc.status_code=14, exception '14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET', and the frontend route spans returned HTTP 500. product-catalog's own server-side spans carried no errors and kept p95 ~1.9 ms while its call counts collapsed (3032/5m to 0), consistent with network-level disruption rather than application failure. No pod restart or rollout occurred in otel-demo (all pods Running, 0 restarts, all deployments 1/1 ready; frontend-proxy pod started 00:26:29Z), and the flagd feature-flag config read has every flag, including productCatalogFailure, set to defaultVariant 'off'. Conclusion is partial: the chaos objects (Schedule/NetworkChaos) are chaos-mesh custom resources not readable with the available tools, so the injected delay parameters and schedule creation time could not be verified, and the alert rule itself could not be retrieved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span errors: sum by span_name/status_code increase over 5m of traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name=frontend-proxy shows span_name=ingress,status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0 for the point at 01:03:22, then 288.89 (01:05:22), 582.22 (01:07:22), 580 (01:09:22), 607.11 (01:11:22), 596.67 (01:13:22) and 362.41 (01:15:22); earlier points were 0–5 per 5m.

frontend-proxy ingress latency: histogram_quantile(0.95) over traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress"} was ~375–517 ms at every sampled point from 00:41:22 to 01:03:22 and 15000 ms at every point from 01:05:22 to 01:15:22.

frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d logs contain repeated '504 UT response_timeout' entries with a 15000 ms upstream duration for GET /api/products/<id>, GET /api/recommendations?productIds=..., POST /api/checkout and 308/200 for /api/data, tagged with upstream 'frontend' (e.g. 01:10:16.969754Z GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N -> 504 UT response_timeout 15000; 01:10:22.460539Z POST /api/checkout -> 504 UT response_timeout 15000), while POST /api/cart returned 200 in the same period.

frontend-proxy error spans are 15 s timeouts: sampled frontend-proxy ingress spans carry status_tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR with duration_us about 15,000,000 (e.g. span 74de5b9996572945 = 15001077 us), and their child 'router frontend egress' spans (span 74e96c7a13794156) last 15000678 us with error="true", http.status_code="0".

Whole trace f2dd787005542001fa63d417d7a7940d shows load-generator GET (15002511 us, error=true, http.status_code=504) -> frontend-proxy ingress (15001077 us, 504) -> frontend-proxy egress (15000678 us, error true) -> frontend GET span 51e6a9f4221b0b88 lasting 15000142 us; the frontend span recorded http.status_code=200, so the proxy aborted at its 15 s timeout while the frontend request was still in flight.

frontend itself records errors: service_name=frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase was 0 at the 01:04:22 point and reached 121.11 per 5m (01:09:22) and 204.27 per 5m (01:14:22); operation GET /api/products/{productId} stopped returning UNSET spans (1241.11 per 5m at 01:03:22, 641.11 at 01:05:22, 60 at 01:07:22, 0 from 01:11:22) and POST /api/checkout ERROR appeared at 48.89 per 5m (01:11:22) rising to 68.15 (01:15:22).

The failing dependency edge is frontend -> product-catalog: frontend spans grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=14, tag grpc.error_message='14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET', with durations 1250599–2061846 us, and their parent frontend spans 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]' end in HTTP 500 with exception.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET'.

product-catalog's own spans did not degrade: histogram_quantile(0.95) of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket for service_name=product-catalog stayed at 1.90–1.99 ms at every point from 00:44:22 to 01:09:22, and product-catalog carried no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series; at the same time its span volume fell from 3032.33 per 5m (01:02:22 point) to 2284.44, then 98.89 and 0 (01:14:22).

Chaos-mesh NetworkChaos objects in namespace chaos-mesh named otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-jj42n, -6rtdg, -bx27q, -x5l64, -b5dxg, -gjgf2, -d9vpw, -26dqc, -hcwrz each logged reason=Started at 01:02:21Z, 01:03:21Z, 01:04:21Z, 01:05:21Z, 01:06:21Z, 01:07:21Z, 01:08:21Z, 01:09:21Z and 01:10:21Z respectively, with reason=Applied message 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9', followed ~55 s later by reason=TimeUp 'Time up according to the duration' and reason=Recovered 'Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9'.

The recurring NetworkChaos objects are spawned by a chaos-mesh Schedule named otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay in namespace chaos-mesh: its events (reason=Spawned) read 'Create new object: otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-jj42n' at 01:02:21Z through 'otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-hcwrz' at 01:10:21Z, one per minute.

No restart or rollout explains the error burst: every otel-demo pod is Running and Ready, frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d has restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-18T00:26:29Z, product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 has restartCount 0, and all 21 otel-demo deployments report 1 desired / 1 ready replica.
Service endpoints for the call path exist at query time: endpoints frontend 100.96.1.181:8080, frontend-proxy 100.96.4.150:8080 and product-catalog 100.96.4.247:8080.

The flagd feature-flag ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) as read has every flag at defaultVariant 'off', including productCatalogFailure (defaultVariant 'off', description 'Fail product catalog service on a specific product'), adFailure, cartFailure and paymentFailure.

The frontend-proxy 504s are caused by the recurring chaos-mesh network fault applied to the product-catalog pod: requests that traverse product-catalog (product detail, recommendations, checkout) hang and the proxy aborts at its 15 s timeout, while cart-only paths keep returning 200. The Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay is the object that repeatedly applies this fault.

Feature-flag fault injection (flagd) was rejected as the cause: every flag in flagd-config is defaultVariant 'off', including productCatalogFailure, so no fault flag was enabled in the configuration that was read.

A frontend-proxy restart, crash or rollout was rejected as the cause: the pod has restartCount 0 and started at 00:26:29Z (before the window), no previous container log stream exists, and deployment frontend-proxy reports 1/1 ready replicas.

An application-level failure inside product-catalog was rejected: product-catalog's own span duration p95 remained ~1.9 ms and it emitted no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, so the disruption is on the network path to/from the pod, not in its request handling.

Read the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and its generated NetworkChaos objects (spec.action/delay, target selector, duration, scheduler) to confirm the injected delay value and when the schedule was created, then suspend or delete that schedule if the fault was not intentional.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule from the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration used for otel-demo, since the registered Prometheus returned no rule named RequestErrorRate and the reported value 1.422222222222222 could not be reproduced from frontend-proxy error spans (0.5037/s at 01:04:22Z).

gaps: The chaos-mesh objects themselves (kind Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and the NetworkChaos otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-* instances) are not in the readable Kubernetes kind list, so their spec could not be read: the injected delay value, the target selector, the per-experiment duration and the schedule's creation time are unknown; only their events were available.

Chaos events are recorded only through source_end_at 2026-11-18T01:10:21Z; whether the schedule kept spawning experiments after 01:10:21Z is unknown, although frontend-proxy error spans were still ~362 per 5m at the 01:15:22 point.

The RequestErrorRate alert rule could not be retrieved (list_prometheus_rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so the metric/expression behind the reported value 1.422222222222222 is unverified; an equivalent frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate query gave 0.5037/s at 01:04:22Z.
frontend container logs for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-64blr returned no lines (bytes_read 0) for 01:00–01:19Z, so frontend's runtime errors are known only from spans.

product-catalog container log filtering (filter 'product-catalog|deadline|timeout|error') matched none of 1769 lines read and the stream read through only 01:09:35Z, so the application-log side of product-catalog during the fault is unevidenced.
A networkpolicy listing over all namespaces returned no items, so it cannot be stated whether a policy blocks traffic; networkpolicy state at incident time is unknown.
fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n7vmf shows restartCount 2 with Created/Started events at 00:58:37Z, inside the window; this change is not tied to the frontend-proxy 504s and its cause is unexplained.
recommendation spans fell to 0 per 5m from the 01:09:22 point onward with no error series observed; whether recommendation failed on its own calls to product-catalog is unchecked.
checkout service spans carried no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series; only frontend-side client spans (grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) show errors, so internal checkout failure is unverified.
Sampled traces and span metrics are not a complete request graph or failure rate; omitted spans and requests outside the sampled window remain unknown.
next_steps: Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule and NetworkChaos resources (kubectl get schedule,networkchaos -n chaos-mesh) to record the exact delay parameters, target pod selector and creation timestamp.
Compare the alert rule definition in the Alertmanager-owning Prometheus with the traces_span_metrics_calls_total series used here to reconcile the reported 1.4222 error-rate value.
Check whether the chaos schedule was created by an operator or test harness, and whether the same schedule targets other services outside the sampled event list.
Review fraud-detection's 3 container starts around 00:58:37Z separately, since that restart is unrelated to (and does not explain) the product-catalog network fault.
